account:
It is six in the morning on day 1, and I have just woken at home. I have not yet seen what anyone is doing today. My appointments include office business at eight, a grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home, council letters at one, tea with my neighbour at three, office at four-thirty, and a great hall lighting inspection at six. I should read the appointment book this morning to confirm them.

The unusual business is the builder's installation of eight lanterns in the great hall and the invitation to inspect them this evening. The builder said no accounts or approvals were needed, only my opinion. The secretary entered the inspection after I approved the time. It may simply be an improvement to the hall; I have no confirmed evidence of another purpose.

There has also been vague chatter about lights or decorations at the bakery. My neighbour identified Townsfolk 02 as the source, but said their talk of a bridge or port change did not fit the conversation and could not establish what they actually witnessed. The neighbour had seen no decorations, and reported that the baker knew of no celebration. The secretary likewise had no confirmed information. I feel there might be preparations I do not understand, but a celebration or any connection between the bakery chatter and the hall lighting remains speculation.

Town account figures were not available yesterday. I do not know who holds them, and asked the secretary to check existing council records for the responsible person and set aside any council letters. No correspondence or further business had been delivered when the secretary last clearly reported.
